title: Profile budget policy when a source pinned by three profiles grows (design question)
description: Filed from LCLI-698 note (2), unstamped for opum-doc. docs/reference/cli-contract.md is pinned by three agent profiles (verification, implementation, review). LCLI-677 grew it (12 rows in the section 2.1 kind registry) and moved only the verification budget (96000 to 96400), leaving the implementation over-capacity warning in place and widening its deficit from about 481 to about 1063 over the 108000 budget; the review budget 63000 absorbed the growth. QUESTION: should each profile budget move whenever a pinned source grows, or does a source pinned by three profiles argue for something else -- a shared budget rule, or a warning the change author is expected to resolve? UNSTAMPED: no assignee, no acceptance criteria; opum-doc decides.

acceptanceCriteria.text: When a source pinned by several profiles grows, EVERY pinning profile budget moves in the same change, not only the one the author edited.
Check: the gate FAILS if ANY pinning profile is over capacity, not only the profile the author touched, and it reports each pinning profile deficit by name.
A test pins the multi-profile gate: growing a source pinned by several profiles with an over-capacity profile other than the edited one fails the gate and names it.

implementationNotes:
Implemented DEC-172 (4at) as a NEW error-tier rule, `agent-profile-pin-capacity`. Own rule name and own fixed error severity (`AGENT_PROFILE_PIN_CAPACITY_SEVERITY = "error"`); DEC-11's `AGENT_PROFILE_CAPACITY_SEVERITY` is untouched, so LCLI-646's flip stays its own one-line change. For each over-capacity profile that NAMES at least one source another profile also names (in `pinned` OR `sources`), `lore check` FAILS (exit 6) with one finding per such profile, naming its shared sources and its deficit. New surface lives in `src/core/check.ts` (`agentProfilePinCapacityFindings`, `AGENT_PROFILE_PIN_CAPACITY_SEVERITY`, the rule union) and `src/commands/check.ts` (the reference -> naming-profiles map, built from the loaded snapshot).

AC1 applied to this repo in the SAME change: `implementation.toml` 108000 -> 111000 and `verification.toml` 96523 -> 97000. Both were pushed over capacity by this change's own doc edits to `docs/reference/cli-contract.md`, a source both profiles name — the rule's own incident shape (LCLI-677). Numbers set: implementation 111000, verification 97000 (requirements were ~110024 and ~96722); `lore check` reports "4 read, 0 over capacity" and exits 0.

Tests in `test/check-agent-profile-capacity.test.ts`: the failing case (a source two profiles name, "edited" raised to fit and "other" left over capacity -> exit 6 and a finding naming `other`, never `edited`); the both-ways control (both budgets raised -> passes); the scoped control (a source only ONE profile names -> DEC-11's per-profile warning, NOT the new error, exit 0). Falsification: removing the gate call from `commands/check.ts` reddens exactly the failing case (verified), so the test earns the gate rather than passing beside it.

Gates: `bun test` 5007 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lore check` (exit 0) all green.
finalSummary: Implemented DEC-172 (4at) as a NEW error-tier rule, `agent-profile-pin-capacity`, for the multi-profile case only: a source several profiles name (in `pinned` or `sources`) fails `lore check` (exit 6) when any pinning profile is over capacity — one finding per such profile, naming the shared sources and its deficit, so a change must move EVERY pinning profile's budget, not only the one it edited. DEC-11's `agent-profile-capacity` warning and its held flip (LCLI-646) are untouched. AC1 applied live in the same change: `implementation.toml` 108000->111000 and `verification.toml` 96523->97000 (this change's own cli-contract.md edits pushed both over). Tests + a mutation falsification in `test/check-agent-profile-capacity.test.ts`. Gates green: bun test 5007 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, lint, typecheck, lore check exit 0. Delivered under opum-control job-1f76lcf.
